ohms_law.title: Ohm's Law & Resistance
ohms_law.summary: Comprehensive engineering analysis of Ohm's Law & Resistance in electrical network theory.
ohms_law.memory_trick: 🧠 Memory Trick for Ohm's Law & Resistance: Remember the governing conservation law: Energy in = Energy out!
ohms_law.theory: In electrical network theory, Ohm's Law & Resistance forms the mathematical foundation for analyzing circuit behavior.
derivation_steps: Step 1: Identify circuit branch parameters and node connections for Ohm's Law & Resistance.
Step 2: Apply governing physical laws (KCL/KVL or Theorem definition).
Step 3: Formulate algebraic loop/node matrix equations.
Step 4: Solve system equations for branch currents and node voltages.
important_formulas: Power Equation: P = V \cdot I = I^2 \cdot R

examples.problem: A circuit under Ohm's Law & Resistance has V_s = 12V and R_1 = 4 ohms, R_2 = 6 ohms in series. Find total current and power.
examples.solution: Total R = R_1 + R_2 = 10 ohms. Current I = 12V / 10 = 1.2A. Total Power P = 12V * 1.2A = 14.4W.

common_mistakes: Forgetting reference polarities (+/-) when writing KVL mesh equations.
Not deactivating independent current sources (open circuit) when computing R_th or Superposition.
ohms_law.professor_notes: Professor's Tip: Always double-check node voltage references before formulating nodal matrices for Ohm's Law & Resistance.
